final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with Cabinet signatures Friday (Canada/Mexico) and U.S. Congressional notification Monday morning, locking labor enforcement (violator-pays tariff deductions), 3.5% dairy TRQ phased over 18 months, 75% auto RVC with 18-month model-year phase-in, Chapter 19 preserved, and review-based sunset. October 15th House vote locked. Any amendment resets the clock and kills the deal.
minority_objections: Mexico initially resisted unannounced U.S. inspections in factories as sovereignty violation
Supply-chain manufacturers warned immediate RVC implementation would trigger pre-emptive reshoring
Labor union demanded explicit violator-pays language to prevent downstream liability shifting
key_conflicts: Mexico sovereignty vs. U.S. labor enforcement inspection regime (resolved via trilateral panel)
Canada dairy supply management vs. U.S. agriculture market access demands (resolved at 3.5% TRQ)
Hard sunset clause business uncertainty vs. Congressional accountability (resolved via review mechanism)
Immediate vs. phased auto RVC compliance timeline (resolved at 18-month model-year basis)
key_concessions: Mexico accepted trilateral labor panel with binding tariff deductions (1% per violation, 5% cap) targeting violator entities
Canada accepted 3.5% dairy market opening phased over 18 months while preserving supply management framework
U.S. accepted review-based sunset instead of hard termination clause
Auto industry received 18-month model-year phase-in for 75% RVC instead of day-one implementation
USTR committed to non-amendable treaty text in Congressional notification, resetting clock if modified
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement preservation (never negotiable)
Canada: Supply management framework protection (accepted limited access only)
Mexico: No unilateral U.S. inspections in Mexican factories (accepted trilateral panel)
U.S. Congress: Enforceable labor violations with automatic tariff penalties (locked in treaty text)
All parties: No treaty amendments during 60-day Congressional review without resetting trilateral consent
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Parliamentary ratification timeline in Canada beyond Cabinet signature
Mexican domestic political capacity to implement labor inspections at scale
Supply-chain disruption during 18-month transition if existing model lines mid-cycle
Dispute panel interpretation of 'violator entity' in complex multi-tier supply chains
Enforcement capacity of trilateral labor panel without permanent secretariat
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional committee attempts to amend labor/dairy language despite notification constraints
Canadian Parliament rejection if domestic dairy lobby mobilizes against 3.5% access
Auto industry capex freeze if October 15th vote slips past recess
Mexican labor enforcement implementation gaps triggering early tariff deductions
Review-mechanism politics at 6-year renewal creating new sunset uncertainty
uncertainty_notes: Effective date definition for RVC phase-in (Congressional vote vs. 90-day post-ratification) remained ambiguous in final exchanges. Trilateral labor panel's operational structure, staffing, and inspection frequency undefined. Canadian Parliamentary vote timeline and whip count not surfaced. Mexican Cabinet signature same-day commitment conditional on Canada moving first.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC compliance timeline drove concrete 18-month model-year phase-in concession; auto industry threatened pre-emptive reshoring without it; locked in notification letter as non-negotiable
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Violator-pays tariff deduction mechanism (1% per violation, 5% cap) became the core enforcement unlock; Congress made it ratification prerequisite; drove trilateral panel structure and treaty text language
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: 3.5% TRQ phased access became the explicit price for Canada signing; U.S. agriculture stated 'won't support package without it'; locked in notification letter as core commitment
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'stays off the table' and 'never negotiable' but did not block progress or extract concessions on it; acknowledged as protected, then set aside
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Review-based sunset replaced hard termination clause as 'genuine breakthrough' that unlocked package convergence; eliminated investment freeze concern that drove business opposition
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: October 15th House vote deadline drove compressed Friday-Monday signature/notification timeline; Congress demanded non-amendable text or 'deal dies'; shaped every final concession
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Raised repeatedly (18-month retooling, capex freeze risk, reshoring hedge) but did not change core RVC number or enforcement; acknowledged as transition cost, then accommodated via phase-in timing
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR's 'sign now or we proceed trilaterally without you' ultimatum and Mexico's 'we're ready same-day' commitment explicitly pressured Canada to accept dairy/labor package or face exclusion
